description.value: We used a rewarded drug cue-reactivity task to examine whether oral methylphenidate alters anterior cingulate function and associated task performance in individuals with cocaine-use disorders and healthy controls.

spans.text: In the current functional MRI study, we used a rewarded drug cue-reactivity task previously shown to be associated with hypoactivations in both major ACC subdivisions (implicated in default brain function) in CUD compared with healthy controls.

value: We hypothesized that oral MPH will attenuate ACC hypoactivations and improve associated performance during a salient cognitive task in individuals with cocaine-use disorders (CUD).

spans.text: Similar to other fMRI tasks of emotion, the two word types were presented in a blocked on-off or off-on order (i.e., drug-neutral or neutral-drug) ( 50 ) and counterbalanced between subjects.
